points: The Nov 19 Q3 print will show whether the FY2027 guidance Brinker laid out in its August release is already translating into July-September sales and traffic, or if the ramp is still a back-half story.
With FY1 EPS growth essentially flat and FY2 EPS growth consensus at ~34.6%, the print needs to confirm the earnings inflection is moving from Q3 into Q4 and early FY2027 rather than stalling.
BJRI, CAKE, BROS and SHAK all report before Nov 19, so their demand, pricing and cost commentary will set the read-through table; strong peer prints would support the EAT long case.
The valuation flag is fair at ~0.8x the restaurant theme median P/E, so the long case rests on execution: Q3 must keep FY2 estimates credible without relying on multiple expansion.
The 90-day revenue estimate is up +5.86%, but the last 30 days saw 2 upgrades and 5 downgrades; the print needs to reverse near-term analyst skepticism and show the top-line beat path is intact.
If Chili's traffic and menu initiatives are gaining share, the following quarters set up well because FY2027 guidance implies a steep ramp and any Q3 confirmation de-risks the FY2 EPS estimate.
Watch management's cost commentary on commodities and labor; stable or improving cost trends make the margin leverage behind FY2's ~34.6% EPS growth more achievable.
watch: Chili's comparable sales / traffic growth: sustained or accelerating positive trend supports the long.
Restaurant-level or operating margin: year-over-year expansion supports the long.
FY2027 guidance / Q4 implied EPS trajectory: reaffirmed or raised outlook supports the long.
Post-print analyst revisions: net upgrades after 2 up/5 down in the past 30 days supports the long.
